bullets.text: A landslide known as the Ashfell Slide struck the mining region of Dreth on 14 March 2026, affecting the Withel terraces and Cranmoor.
The slide began as a bench failure that damaged the lower road below the Withel terraces within the first hours.
No casualties were reported in the first four hours, with about 60 households evacuated from the Withel terraces.
Authorities issued a warning for the Withel terraces and Cranmoor and evacuated residents from both areas, with attribution of the slide contested.
A bench failure occurs on the Ashfell slope and damages the lower road.
A warning is issued for the Withel terraces and Cranmoor.
About 60 households are evacuated from the Withel terraces.
Residents move out of the Withel terraces and Cranmoor as the evacuation continues to the end of the window.
The bench failure of the Ashfell slide damaged the lower road below the Withel terraces.
About 60 households were evacuated from the Withel terraces after the warning was issued.
Residents were also moved out of Cranmoor as part of the evacuation.
A warning was issued for the Withel terraces and Cranmoor after the bench failure.
